summary: Dedicated pool throughput collapse triggered by background snapshot IO causing prefetch starvation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Acme Health reports sustained throughput collapse (p50 and p99 increases) on their dedicated pool starting 2026-03-13 09:12 UTC during a scheduled background KV-cache snapshot job. Impact:
- Production inference latency spiked from 120ms p50 to 800ms p50 and p99 > 6s for 20 minutes.
- Several requests hit 504/5xx fallback and some requests folded over to fallback model variants.
Environment:
- Dedicated capacity: pool:d-acme-01 (8x A100s), autoscaler configured with burst buffer, prefetch enabled, persistent KV cache.
- Snapshotter cron runs daily at 09:00 UTC with concurrent checkpointing across multiple tenants.
Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Snapshot cron starts; background snapshot writer begins large NVMe reads and writes.
2) Snapshotter IO saturates host NVMe and incites kernel throttling visible as elevated iowait on host metrics.
3) Prefetch worker latencies increase; KV prefetch backpressure forms and allocator delays GPU attach due to blocked prefetch slots.
4) Autoscaler interprets queue growth as demand spike then attempts scale-up which stalls on GPU attach timeouts.
5) Throughput collapses until snapshot completes and IO normalizes.
Observed logs & traces:
- Serving runtime logs show repeated "prefetch_timeout" and "kv-cache-slow-read" errors around 09:12 UTC.
- Node metrics: nvme_io_util at 95%, load average spikes, dmesg entries showing ext4 writeback delays.
- Autoscaler events: repeated "attach_timeout" and "allocation-retry" between 09:13-09:18 UTC.
- Customer reported increased 5xx counts and application-level timeouts.
Expected behavior:
- Background snapshot activity should not cause host-level IO saturation for production inference tenants on dedicated pools. Prefetch/backpressure should gracefully rate-limit snapshot traffic or the snapshot process should yield to inference priority.
Attachments:
- Links to dashboards: 
  * Serving latency dashboard: https://console.redwood.local/dashboards/serving/pool-d-acme-01
  * Host IO metrics: https://console.redwood.local/dashboards/infra/nvme-usw2
comments: 2026-03-13 Priya Sharma: Ticket opened after customer escalation via support@. Included initial telemetry and ask for SRE triage.

2026-03-13 Marcus Lee (SRE): Noted correlation with snapshotter cron. Observed NVMe saturation on host group hostpool-usw2-3. Marking as P1 and requesting temporary mitigation. Assigning to Ethan for coordination with customer and on-call storage team.

2026-03-13 Ethan Brooks: Confirmed we can throttle snapshotter for Acme Health's pool as immediate mitigation. Preparing runbook steps to pause snapshot cron for 30 minutes and reschedule off-peak. Need customer approval for transient snapshot delay.
2026-03-13 Customer (Acme Health, Alice Zhang): Approves pausing snapshot for 40 minutes. Impact acceptable as long as a delayed snapshot completes within the next maintenance window.

2026-03-13 Marcus Lee: Implemented host-level IO niceness change on affected nodes and applied cgroup io.weight reduction to snapshotter process on the host. Observed NVMe util drop from 95% to 40% and prefetch latencies returning to baseline within 6 minutes.
2026-03-14 Priya Sharma: Customer confirmed throughput stabilized after mitigation and no further 5xx observed overnight. Moving investigation to root cause analysis and follow-up recommendations.

2026-03-14 Ethan Brooks: Drafting long-term recommendations: snapshot staggering per-tenant, snapshot IO throttling, and scheduler-affinity to avoid collocating heavy snapshotters with low-latency dedicated pools. Will propose changes to snapshotter team and propose a config flag to mark "inference-critical" pools.
investigation_notes: Timeline correlation strong: snapshot start at 09:02 UTC, degradation begins 09:12 UTC (small lag where prefetch backlog ramps).
Host-level evidence: nvme_io_util and iowait spike coincident with kernel ext4 writeback warnings. No GPU driver faults. Kernel reported BIO writeback throttling.
Autoscaler was performing expected actions; attach timeouts were caused by blocked prefetch paths (not by scheduler permission errors).

Reproduced locally on staging by running a concurrent snapshot writer and a prefetch-heavy synthetic workload: same pattern: prefetch latency up -> allocation delays -> throughput fall. Suggests systemic IO interference between snapshotter and prefetch worker.
resolution:
Mitigation applied (2026-03-13): paused snapshot cron for Acme Health's pool and applied host-level IO throttling to snapshotter processes via cgroups; observed recovery within 10 minutes. Temporary fix accepted by customer.
Follow-up actions (planned):
- Snapshotter team to implement tenant-aware snapshot staggering and an io.limit flag for snapshot jobs (action: RFC + rollout, owner: storage team).
- Add scheduler constraint to avoid placing snapshot writers on hosts serving inference-critical dedicated pools (owner: scheduler team).
- Add alerting rule for sustained NVMe util > 80% on nodes with active prefetch traffic (owner: infra monitoring).
- Consider exposing a "snapshot_safety" pool-level config for customers to opt-in to strict throttling on background maintenance (owner: product).
